cards.title: What are Interceptors?
cards.content:
Interceptors in Angular

Interceptors sit between your application and the backend. They allow you to intercept and modify HTTP requests and responses globally.

Common use cases include:

  • Attaching authentication tokens to outgoing requests
  • Catching and handling global HTTP errors
  • Logging requests and responses

In modern Angular, functional interceptors (HttpInterceptorFn) are preferred over the older class-based HttpInterceptor.

cards.title: Modifying Requests
cards.content:
Cloning Requests

HttpRequest objects are immutable. To modify a request (like adding a header), you must clone it.

export const authInterceptor: HttpInterceptorFn = (req, next) => {
  const authReq = req.clone({
    setHeaders: { Authorization: `Bearer my-token` }
  });
  return next(authReq);
};

cards.title: Error Handling & Retry
cards.content:
Handling Errors Globally

Interceptors can also process responses. Since next(req) returns an Observable, you can use RxJS operators like catchError and retry.

export const errorInterceptor: HttpInterceptorFn = (req, next) => {
  return next(req).pipe(
    retry(2),
    catchError(error => {
      console.error('HTTP Error:', error);
      return throwError(() => error);
    })
  );
};
